newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares at another record in busy trading.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares at another record in busy trading.

text.p: Egyptian share prices notched up another record and rose 1.28 percent on Wednesday as investors descended full-force on the market after the four-day public holiday, brokers said.

The Capital Market Authority's all-share index closed at 411.53 points, its 17th highest level in as many trading days. Broad-based trading brought the day's turnover up to a high 90.49 million pounds ($26.6 million).
"Prices are up again and that's a good indication. Everyone thought the market would fall after the Eid al-Fitr (Islamic feast) holiday but it's holding up," said broker Elwi Taymour of Hermes/EFG.
But despite profit-taking in some sectors, brokers said the market was not yet due for a correction as foreign and local investors continue to pour in funds.

"It went up sharply but we don't expect it to fall rapidly. There is still room for growth and there will be slight changes and some stabilising but the uptrend is still strong," broker Youssef Khalil of Delta EAB.
The presence of cash-rich foreign investors was most felt in the banking sector, brokers said.

Misr International Bank/MIBANK rose 32.07 to 673.62 pounds in trade worth 9.1 million pounds as foreign investors exchanged tranches of shares. The bank has proposed tranfering some shares through a global depository receipt offering and that had also spurred trade, the brokers said.
National Societe General Bank also rose 50.23 to 1,054.98 in similar deals while Commerical International Bank gained 31.5 pounds to 661.5 but in smaller deals.
Investors also targetted the cement and milling firms but prices ended mixed. Helwan Portland Cement was the day's most active share, rising 0.51 to 80.51 in heavy volume of 10.67 million.
"This is the cheapest cement stock currently on the market and the firm has good growth potential. It's definitely on our buy list," said Taymour.
Amriyah Cement was also among the day's 10 most active stocks but ended 2.4 pounds down to 94 pounds.
Profit-taking hit some firms in the popular milling sector and brokers predicted price falls in others which ended the day firmer.
"It's natural that investors recoup their gains and all those firms rising are showing signs of overheating. They're bound to fall," Taymour said.
North Cairo Flour Mills fell 7.00 pounds to 200 in trading worth almost four million pounds while Central Egypt Flour Mills rose 1.1 to 82.25 in similar volume.
Abu Qir Fertilisers and Chemical Industries was also active for the second day running and rose 4.9 pounds to 102.9 in what a broker described as "mystery trading".
"Foreign investors are not allowed to buy this stock because of a clause in its by-laws and there's no reason for this rise. Maybe someone is buying the stock to retail it," Taymour said.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 687.29 points from 673.89 points on Tuesday and the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 270.96 from 268.82 points.
Out of the 87 shares traded, 56 gained, 17 lost and 14 ended the day unchanged.
$1 = 3.40 pounds
